R0037.title: Third-Party Account Aggregation
R0037.definition: Using a third-party application as a proxy to centrally manage account credentials for multiple applications.
R0037.description: Compiling credentials and information from multiple application accounts into another system. A single user can use this aggregation application to consolidate information from multiple applications, or consolidate information from multiple users of a single application — for example, e-commerce migration tools or ticket-grabbing applications.
R0037.influence: For users, there is a risk of sensitive information leakage; for the system, there is a risk of platform data loss and increased system request pressure.

references.title: OWASP Automated Threat: OAT020 Account Aggregation

observables: A single account issues logins and data pulls from multiple geographic regions via non-official clients within a short window
The device fingerprint on login requests does not match the account's historical patterns, accompanied by batch queries across multi-platform order, product, and ticket data
Characteristic User-Agents or custom headers of third-party aggregation apps appear on login and data synchronization endpoints
A single account pulls core business data such as orders, products, and tickets at high frequency, with volume far exceeding normal browsing
Shortly after login, the account concurrently accesses endpoints across multiple unrelated business modules
